contextual.summary: Imperial's contextual admissions route for UK (Home) applicants can give a guaranteed interview and a guaranteed offer at the department's minimum entry level, plus an August reconsideration pool.
contextual.typicalReduction: Guaranteed offer at the department's minimum entry level (for Economics, Finance and Data Science that is A*AA)

criteria.detail: Care leaver or have spent time in care under a local authority
Home postcode in England's Index of Multiple Deprivation quintile one
Currently receive UK government funded free school meals, or received them in the last six years up to the end of your final year at school or college

Home postcode in POLAR4 quintile 1 or 2 — counts only together with one of: first in immediate family to go to university; English school with key stage 5 performance below Imperial's 20% percentile threshold; UK school with a free school meals percentile above Imperial's 80% threshold
First in your immediate family to attend university or higher education (counts only with a POLAR4 quintile 1 or 2 postcode)

Attend an English school where key stage 5 performance is below Imperial's 20% percentile threshold, or a UK school where the free school meals percentile is above Imperial's 80% threshold (counts only with a POLAR4 quintile 1 or 2 postcode)

contextual.rulesText: Applicants with Home fee status are eligible if one of these applies: care experience; IMD quintile 1 postcode; free school meals (now or in the last six years); or a POLAR4 quintile 1 or 2 postcode plus one of first-generation, low-performing school (KS5) or high-FSM school.

programmes.name: mA*ths Online Programme (Year 12 cohort)
programmes.summary: An outreach programme funded by Imperial: online courses, online mentoring and masterclasses at Imperial to help A-level Maths students aim for an A* in Mathematics.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 UK state school students studying at least three A-levels including Maths, with at least grade 6 in GCSE Maths and Sciences, planning maths-heavy university courses (such as Economics); priority for under-represented backgrounds.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Funded by Imperial to support UK state school students from backgrounds under-represented at university. Priority if in care or estranged; also assessed: young carer, family income below £50,000, free school meals/pupil premium, parents didn't attend university, POLAR4 quintile 1–2 or IMD quintile 1 area, school with high free school meals or below-average attainment, asylum seeker/refugee or Gypsy, Traveller, Roma, Showmen and Boaters. Must be in Year 12, taking 3+ A-levels including Maths, GCSE 6+ in Maths and Sciences (2+ science GCSEs), capable of an A in A-level Maths, willing to travel to Imperial up to twice a year on weekends. You don't have to live in London.
benefits: Online courses (MOOCs) matched to A-level Maths
Masterclasses at Imperial with academics and MEI
programmes.cost: Funded by Imperial College London (page doesn't state a fee)

runs.text: Introductory masterclass 16 January 2027; two seven-week online courses in the spring/summer terms; closing masterclass (page lists 8 May 2026)

admissionsTest.name: TMUA
admissionsTest.effect: You must sit the TMUA to be considered. There is no minimum score, but a higher score may make your application more competitive; it is weighed with the rest of your application when deciding interviews and offers. It doesn't change the offer grades.

source.evidence: We do not have a minimum score to achieve, though a higher score may make your application more competitive.

alternativeOffers.conditions: Guaranteed offer at the department's minimum entry level (A*AA, including A* in Maths, for this course) if you're eligible for Imperial's contextual admissions route, are predicted at least AAA, show clear motivation for the subject in your personal statement, and score above the department's minimum in its admissions test and/or interview
